text:
tay: quick check — we got a bug report where clients send both `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `X-Api-Key: sk_...` plus `X-Project-Id`. Which header wins in multi-tenant flow?

matt: by current design, we prefer `X-Api-Key` over `Authorization` for user-facing keys. org/project scope uses `X-Project-Id` when present.

sofia: is that documented? clients are hitting 400 vs 401 inconsistently. we should standardize response codes.

tay: not well documented, no. reported case: request had expired key in Authorization and valid X-Api-Key — server returned 401 instead of accepting X-Api-Key.

matt: :grimacing: that sounds like short-circuit auth check order in proxy. infra-bot: deploy 2024-11-07-agg-check rerouted auth check ordering last week might be related.

jamie: what should the contract say? my vote: evaluate `X-Api-Key` first, then `Authorization`, then fallback to `x-org-id` resolution only if neither present. callers expect explicit key header to take precedence.

sofia: agree. also we need to define error mapping: missing any key & no project => 401. invalid key => 401. key present but lacks project access => 403. ambiguous/multiple keys => prefer explicit header and ignore token after logging telemetry.

matt: corner: when both headers present and one is expired, we should still accept the valid one. Do not return 401 if another valid credential is present.

tay: +1. that matches how SDKs work — SDKs set `X-Api-Key` by default.

sdk-team: can we also add guidance for SDKs to stop inferring `x-project-id` from env automatically? it's causing surprising org-scoping.

jamie: yes, SDK change is small: only send `X-Project-Id` if explicitly provided by user; otherwise leave unset. We'll add a compatibility note for existing customers.

sofia: concrete action items: matt to patch proxy auth order to check `X-Api-Key` before `Authorization` (PR), sdk-team to change SDK default behaviour, and docs update to plain table: header precedence + response codes. I'll open the docs PR.

matt: I'll do a quick patch. expected behavior in tests:
```
# preferred precedence
X-Api-Key -> Authorization -> x-project-id inference -> unauthenticated

# responses
no-cred -> 401
invalid-cred -> 401
valid-cred-but-no-access -> 403
ambiguous-credentials -> accept valid one, log telemetry
```

jamie: should we add a short rotation grace period (30s) where both old and new keys accepted to avoid flapping? existing rotation tickets asked for it.

tay: yes, but implement as a rolling acceptance window on key backend (not proxy) and emit `x-key-rotated:true` header when served with a new key during grace. docs should call this out.

matt: noted. will include a tiny feature flag for safety.

sofia: also: telemetry fields we want: `auth.used_header`, `auth.fallback_used`, `auth.reject_reason` — add to tracking ticket.

sdk-team: will update SDK to stop project inference and bump minor. will link PR here when ready.

tay: thanks all — tagging followups: matt (proxy PR), sofia (docs + tracking ticket), sdk-team (SDK PR). I'll drop a short RFC link in a sec: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2024-auth-headers-ordering :eyes:
